A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same TikTok conspiracy study. Their complete text, equations, figures, tables and appendices support reliable comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: V1 reports original analyses of collected TikTok videos, prevalence estimates, monetization-program comparisons and classifier evaluations.

after.justification: V2 retains these original empirical results and adds qualitative analysis of four misclassified videos.

M1.justification: The hashtag-enrichment formula, ten seeds, CT/DW labeling rule, Whisper transcription, three zero-shot prompting strategies and majority-vote ensemble are retained. Expanded descriptions do not establish a changed classification procedure.

E1.justification: Both use the same U.S. TikTok collection from 2021–2023, samples surrounding the monetization-program launch, and C1–C3 classification scenarios. The nine LOCO seeds plus 'conspiracy' are unchanged. Newly documented English filtering does not establish a changed evaluation population.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain Llama3 8B, Mistral 7B, Gemma 7B, their ensemble and RoBERTa base. Newly cited research does not introduce evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: V1 describes five-fold RoBERTa cross-validation with a 70/30 split. V2 Appendix A.4 instead specifies a 75/25 split and best-model selection, while Section 4.3 inconsistently states 72/25. This changes the reported baseline protocol without establishing that experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: New Appendix A.6 examines two false negatives and two false positives shared by all three LLMs. Existing transcript-length analyses, sampling diagnostics and Whisper validation remain; their relocation does not constitute additional analysis.

E5.justification: V1 explicitly averages results across five RoBERTa folds; v2 removes that replication and aggregation description while retaining confidence intervals and identical uncertainty values. Both retain the same 25 LLM seeds. V2 leaves the basis of the baseline uncertainty less clear.

E6.justification: Table 2's 84 numerical entries and matched performance plots are unchanged. V2 adds four error cases and reports the transcript-length comparison as p < 0.001 instead of p < 0.01. Its C3 underperformance statement switches from precision to recall, unsupported by the retained plot. Figure 2 also introduces a pre-program count of 42 while the text retains 39.

T1.justification: The hashtag-similarity formula and Good-Turing and maximum-likelihood estimators remain mathematically equivalent. V2 adds explanatory prose but no new formal assumptions, derivations or proofs.

C1.justification: V2 explicitly claims the first systematic analysis of TikTok conspiracy theories and foregrounds the absence of a conspiracy-specific monetization effect. The main prevalence and LLM-versus-RoBERTa claims remain substantively unchanged.

C2.justification: V2 explicitly limits the monetization analysis to correlation because of possible confounders, discusses smaller-model performance limitations, and adds hypotheses explaining classification failures. It also introduces the possibility that adversaries could exploit moderation weaknesses.

D1.justification: V2 newly specifies the input template, English-word filtering threshold, 16-core CPU, A6000 GPU with 48 GB memory and approximately ten-hour runtime. It reports access to video-ID/label datasets, whereas v1 provided code and directed readers to contact the authors about data.

R1.justification: Section 2 substantially removes discussions and references concerning Twitter/Facebook trajectories, YouTube recommendations and monetization, and deplatforming. V2 adds positioning around open-weight reproducibility, prompt sensitivity and explanation reliability, and explicitly contrasts its baseline findings with Plaza-del Arco et al. (2024).

P1.justification: Extensive rewriting accompanies substantial reorganization: hashtag validation moves into Methods, detailed sampling moves to the appendix, the prompt definition moves to Appendix B, and limitations become a separate section. Terminology and the results narrative are also revised throughout.

P2.justification: V2 adopts a different conference layout, resizes and reformats figures, moves sampling and transcript-length plots into the appendix, and removes v1 Figure 4's hashtag-count chart. Table headers, caption placement and plot annotations are revised across the document.

improvement.justification: V2 improves exposition, adds failure cases and reproducibility information, and explicitly qualifies causal claims. However, its revised RoBERTa protocol retains identical scores and confidence intervals without explaining their basis, gives conflicting split values, and introduces a C3 recall statement inconsistent with Figure 4. These benefits coexist with material uncertainty in the central model comparison, preventing a reliable net quality judgment.
